consent_microcopy: Launch news, your first invite, and notes from the build — nothing else. Unsubscribe any time.
error_invalid_email: Please check the email address once more.
error_no_consent: Check the consent box and we'll sign you up right away.

error_ratelimit: A lot of requests came in at once. Please try again shortly.
error_generic: Something went wrong for a moment. Please try again shortly.
privacy_intro: Mosmos collects only the minimum information below, for waitlist registration.
privacy_purpose: To share launch news and the first invitation
privacy_consent: Without consent we don't store anything. You can withdraw consent at any time — contact us if you'd like your registration removed.
privacy_optional: Survey answers such as your role and current AI tasks are optional, and are used only to set the order of first invitations.
survey_intro: We use this when setting the invitation order. Thirty seconds.
survey_job_label: What kind of work do you do?
survey_ai_label: What do you mostly use AI for these days?
survey_job_other_label: Other — what kind of work do you do?
survey_task_other_label: Other — tell us what kind of task
survey_done: Thank you. We'll keep this in mind.
confirm_title:
You are registered.
Invitations go out in order as we are ready.
confirm_email_sent: We sent a welcome email — take a look in your inbox.
confirm_care: We invite a few people at a time at first, so we can hear each of them.
confirm_next: We will send word about how it is going now and then.
confirm_world_tagline: Another me, in the digital world
confirm_mos_line: Your name is noted. You will hear when the door opens.
founder_note: I am building Mosmos. I will handle the first invitations myself, and share how it is going rather than only the finished thing.
recruit_title: We are looking for people to build this with
recruit_text: No matching role is fine. Let us talk first.
meta_title: mosmos — a world where my AI grows up
meta_description: Just say it. Mos does the moving. A personal AI for people who research, organise and write things up. We invite the front row first.
hero_tagline: A world where my AI grows up
hero_sub: Just say it. Mos does the moving.
hero_gloss: Mos — settles the goal with you, then hands the work to the AI specialist that fits it
hero_anchor: A personal AI for people who research, organise and write things up
mos_poke_2: That tickles. Shall we get started?
mos_poke_4: Leave your name and I'll remember it.
ache: If getting AI to do the work became work of its own
decide_lead: Mos confirms the goal and hands it to the Mon that fits the job. The Mon runs it; Mos sorts the result and brings it back.
decide_g1: Tell me only what changed in competitors' pricing this week
decide_g2: Pull just the decisions out of yesterday's minutes
decide_g3: Point out the risky clauses in this contract
decide_ask2: Should I match owners to them?
decide_hand: I will hand this to the Mon that covers it.
decide_step3: Sorts the result and brings it back
decide_r1: Two of six pricing pages changed. Only the changed rows are in the table.
decide_r2: Four decisions pulled out. One on hold, carried to the next meeting.
decide_r3: Three high-risk clauses flagged, each with wording to use instead.
decide_cost: The run finished, so it came off for what was used
decide_note: Mos handles the conversation and the routing; a Mon does the running. Mana is charged after the run, for what it used.
watch_title: Write the condition, hear only when it is met
watch_lead: Say what to watch in a sentence. No change that matches means no notification.
watch_memo_hint: One line per condition · checking on its own is not charged
watch_memo_1: Tell me when Mana is running low
watch_memo_2: Tell me if something urgent lands in my inbox
watch_memo_3: Summarise new comments on the shared docs
watch_memo_4: Give me a short note if a competitor page changes
watch_beat_state: Checks every 30 minutes · nothing to report
watch_cron_lead: Work with a fixed time is booked here
watch_note: It runs at the time you set. Leave anything you cannot pin to a time on condition watch.
make_lead: Studio is a canvas: drag nodes in and connect them. No code. Try it on the canvas below.
make_out_v: A report of what it did
make_io_note: A Mon takes work only from Mos and returns results only to Mos. Talking to you is Mos’s job. Every Mon shares that structure, so there is nothing to change here.
make_brain_hint: You do not need model names. Pick the kind of work and it connects to a model that suits it.
make_tier_1_d: Handles short sorting and tidying very quickly.
make_tier_2_d: Balances speed and accuracy across most document work.
make_tier_3_d: Pushes hard judgement calls and their reasoning all the way through.
make_prompt_hint: Split into role, order and rules instead of one blank box
make_pp_role_h: What kind of Mon this is, in a sentence or two
make_pp_role_b: A Mon that reads contracts and terms, and finds the clauses that could be risky. It looks first at the ones people tend to miss.
make_pp_steps_h: The order it works in · number the lines and it follows them
make_pp_steps_b:
1. Find the termination, auto-renewal, liability and confidentiality clauses first.
2. Mark any sentence judged risky, with where it sits in the original.
3. Give the reason in one line.
4. Suggest wording to use instead.
make_pp_keep_h: What it must do, and what it must not
make_pp_keep_b:
Never state this as legal advice.
Quote clauses as written; do not rewrite them.
When something needs checking, ask instead of guessing.
make_pp_all_h: The three pieces joined. Edit in the pieces.
make_palette_hint: Tap to attach, tap again to take it off
make_c_notion_d: Reads pages and writes new ones
make_c_github_d: Reads and writes repos and issues
make_c_ppx_d: Finds it and sorts the sources too
make_c_exa_d: Give it an address, it brings back the text
make_c_browser_d: Uses the web in a window of its own
make_c_s1_d: A Skill bought on the Hub
make_note: Building, storing and publishing are open on every plan. Building itself is not charged.
share_title: Publish the Mons and Skills you build
share_lead: When someone else’s Mos picks your Mon, part of each run’s charge is settled to you. A Skill settles once, at the sale.
share_free_d: The runner pays only the execution cost. Nothing settles to you.
share_paid_d: Part of each run’s charge is settled to you.
share_skill_d: Settled once at purchase. No further settlement on later runs.
share_listed: How it appears in the Hub list
share_mine_desc: Grades the risk of each contract clause and proposes replacement wording.
share_peer_1_m: Sweeps a set topic each week and sums it up
share_peer_2_m: A procedure that splits decided from deferred and attaches owners and dates
share_peer_3_m: Sorts incoming questions by type and priority
share_review_mos: Run records — the Mos that gave it work log completion and format compliance
share_review_patron: Reviews — written by people who used it
share_note: No plan limit on building or publishing. Hub trading and settlement are still being built; we will say when they open.
cost_title: The subscription and the run are billed separately
cost_lead: The subscription covers what stays up whether you use it or not — the account, storage, a scheduled run waiting to fire. Mana is a balance drawn down only when something actually runs. Neither replaces the other.
cost_sub_d: Account, storage, retention of files and run records, a slot for scheduled runs. Things that have to hold even in a month you do not use them.
cost_p1_role: Take one first task all the way through
cost_p2_role: Daily use. Scheduled runs open here.
cost_p3_role: Heavy use. Assigned first when processing backs up.
cost_open: Open regardless of plan — building Mons, storing them, publishing to the Hub
cost_amounts_tbd: The exact storage sizes and retention windows are not settled.
cost_mana: Mana — drawn down only when something runs
cost_mana_d: It recovers the real cost of model calls, tool use, runtime and producing the output.
cost_a1: When a Mon finishes a run
cost_a1_d: Nothing is held before the run. It is charged once afterwards, for what was actually used.
cost_a2: Running a Mon rented from the Hub
cost_a2_d: The charge is the same. Part of it is split off inside as the builder’s settlement.
cost_a3: Buying a Skill on the Hub
cost_a3_d: Once, at purchase. Runs that use it later carry no extra charge.
cost_b1: Building Mons and Skills in Studio
cost_mana_tbd: How much Mana a dollar buys, and the charge per task, are not settled.
cost_note: Prices are not settled. We would rather set them against how the first users react. Once they are, everyone registered hears first.
join_title: Invitations go out in the order you register
join_scarcity: The pilot invites a small number.
trust_care: Your email is used only for launch and pilot news, and notes from the build.
world_island_label: The sky island Mos lives on
make_what_mon: Mon — the AI agent that runs the work
make_what_mon_d: It takes a brief, uses tools and produces the result. Rent one on the Hub; each run is charged in Mana.
make_what_skill: Mon Skill — a procedure document attached to a Mon
make_what_skill_d: It records the order of work and the judgement criteria. It never runs itself; the Mon it is attached to opens and reads it when needed. Buy it once on the Hub and keep it; attaching it is not charged.
make_skill_when_d: The Mon decides from this line alone
make_skill_norun: It is a document, so attaching it is not charged
make_none_yet: Tap a tool to attach it
make_cfg_img_d: How many it makes per run. More images, more charge.
make_cfg_img_fixed_v: Saved to Storage, with links in the written result
make_cfg_exa_d: Unset, it can open any page. Set the range it may read.
make_cfg_notion_d: Read-only leaves your Notion pages unchanged.
make_cfg_gen_note: Generating tools draw extra Mana when they run
recruit_lead: It is early, so we need people who will help set the direction. Three shapes of role below.
recruit_role1_d: Someone who knows one field deeply — research, legal, accounting
recruit_role2_d: Someone to build the product and the business from the start
recruit_role3_d: Someone who likes learning by making
make_c_s1_when: Opened when the document has numbered clauses
make_c_s1_steps: Finds risky clauses, sorts them high / medium / low, and says why
make_c_s2_when: Opened when only the decisions are wanted
make_c_s2_steps: Separates decided from deferred, and attaches an owner and a date
make_canvas_hint: Drag from the palette onto the canvas, or tap to connect it
make_pan_hint: Drag sideways to move the canvas
cost_how: How the charge is worked out
cost_how_d: Not by token count alone. It is costed from the difficulty of the task, which model handled it, how much the cache matched, and how many paid tool calls it made.
cost_how_1: The same task charges less when a lighter model handles it
cost_how_2: It charges less when earlier context is still cached
cost_how_3: Unspent Mana carries into the next month
